study.title: Neuroimaging mechanisms of acupuncture on functional reorganization for post-stroke motor improvement: a machine learning-based functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.study_design: Prospective observational neuroimaging study with machine learning classification; patients grouped by MCID of FMA over 2 weeks; healthy controls included for comparison
study.population: Stroke hemiplegia patients with unilateral motor pathway (basal ganglia and/or corona radiata) injury after ischemic stroke, plus matched healthy controls
study.disease_condition: Ischemic stroke with unilateral motor pathway injury (basal ganglia and/or corona radiata)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) patients with cerebral infarction whose course of the disease is 3 months and conform to the diagnostic criteria of cerebral infarction; (2) right-handed patients; (3) between 40 and 80 years of age, both men and women are eligible; (4) patients in whom the infarct was located in the unilateral basal ganglia and/or the radiation coronal region; (5) the patient with unconscious disorder and the condition is relatively stable; (6) The patient himself or his immediate family members sign the informed consent. HC inclusion: (1) right-handed people; (2) between 40 and 80 years of age, both men and women are eligible; (3) people proved to be healthy by a medical examination; (4) people signed the informed consent and volunteered to participate in the experiment.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) the patient had ever taken psychotropic drugs in the past months; (2) the patient being pregnant or lactation; (3) the patient had a history of neurologic or psychiatric disorders; (4) the patient had any other health problems or poor physical conditions that may influence participation; (5) the patient had any other brain structure damage or abnormalities identified by MRI examinations; (6) the patient had any history of alcohol or drug dependency; (7) the patient had any MRI contraindications. HC: (1) the person had ever taken psychotropic drugs in the past months or had a family genetic history of the mental and nervous system; (2) the person being pregnant or lactation; (3) the person had a history of neurologic or psychiatric disorders; (4) the person had any other health problems or poor physical conditions that may influence participation; (5) the person had any other brain structure damage or abnormalities identified by MRI examinations; (6) the person had any history of alcohol or drug dependency; (7) the person had any MRI contraindications; (8) the person was conducted to other similar research.

conditions.scan_context: Eyes closed, awake, no cognitive tasks; 6 min 10 s scan

conditions.timepoint_exact: Day of enrollment (baseline); 9 min 10 s scan
conditions.scan_context: Acupuncture at Yanglingquan (GB 34) on affected side in patients, left side in HC; 10 s post-onset phase, 1 min manual stimulation, 8 min post-stimulation phase with needle retained

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Acupuncture at Yanglingquan (GB 34) on the affected side
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Outside of the lower leg, in the middle of the concavity of the anterior and inferior parts of the fibula head
interventions.depth_exact: 1–1.5 Cun (about 15–25 mm depending on the height and weight of a participant)
interventions.manipulation_exact: Mild reinforcing-reducing method at the frequency of 1 Hz for 1 min
interventions.needle_retention_exact: 8 min post-stimulation phase with needle remaining inside the leg
interventions.treatment_period_exact: Single MRI session on day of enrollment
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Keep eyes closed and stay awake without performing any cognitive tasks

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Paper does not report deqi/sensory responses as a measured outcome. Deqi was not assessed as a study endpoint.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3.0 Tesla Siemens scanner (MAGNETOM Verio Siemens Medical Systems, Erlangen, Germany)
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: EPI sequence for fMRI; MPRAGE for structural T1
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm (resampled); matrix size 64×64; thickness 3.5 mm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Resting-state: 6 min 10 s; Acupuncture-state: 9 min 10 s; T1: 5 min 10 s
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing & Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI); SPM 12; Matlab 2017a
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Head motion >3 mm translation or a 3° rotation in any direction
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: Global signal regressed out from the time series of all voxels via linear regression
statistical_thresholds_exact: Two-tailed Gaussian random field (GRF) correction: voxel threshold of p<0.01 and cluster threshold of p<0.05
Permutation tests (1,000 permutations) for ML classification
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Bonferroni correction for ANOVA; GRF correction (voxel-p<0.01, cluster-p<0.05) for two-sample t-tests

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Machine learning classification: MCID vs. N-MCID
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: L1-MKL classification using DC maps
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: L1-multi kernel learning machine (L1-MKL) in PRoNTo with leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV); ROI-based MKL using 200 ROIs from Craddock atlas
contrasts.seed_or_roi_exact: 200 ROIs from Craddock whole-brain atlas
contrasts.roi_definition_exact: Craddock et al. (2012) ROI atlas generated by parcellating whole-brain resting-state fMRI data into spatially coherent regions of homogeneous FC
contrasts.statistical_model_exact: L1-MKL supervised learning; nested CV with optimized nested hyperparameter range 2.^[-5:5]
contrasts.thresholding_method_exact: Weight threshold >5% of maximum ROI-weight rank
contrasts.direction_exact: Classification: MCID vs. N-MCID

model_performance_results.target_outcome_exact: MCID vs. N-MCID group classification for motor improvement

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Figure S1 is referenced throughout the paper as containing FC results for ROIs beyond ROI 1 and ROI 2 (which appear in Figure 4). Supplementary Figure S1 was not provided with this PDF. FC results for all 8 ROIs are however tabulated in Table 4, which was fully extracted.
Deqi/sensory responses to acupuncture were not assessed or reported as a study outcome. There are no instruments, scales, or values for acupuncture sensations in this paper.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding/allocation guessing were not measured or reported in this study.
Adverse events were not reported. The paper does not include an adverse event section.

The study reports 'F-value (peak)' in Table 4, but the statistical comparisons are post hoc two-sample t-tests following ANOVA. The values reported as F-value (peak) appear to include both positive and negative values, which may reflect the direction of the t-test. These have been copied exactly as reported. The mapping of 'F-value' to t-statistics is ambiguous in this table.

The paper states images were flipped so all lesions are on the right (positive MNI x-coordinates). Therefore, 'L' in Table 3 refers to 'contralesional hemisphere' and 'R' refers to 'ipsilesional hemisphere'. This is explicitly stated in the table footnote and has been preserved in extraction.

The n_analyzed for FC analyses differs between comparisons. For resting state: MCID (n=28 enrolled, but some may have been excluded) and HC (n=26); for acupuncture state: MCID (n=26), N-MCID (n=15), HC (n=26). The total neuroimaging n for resting state comparisons is not explicitly stated per comparison; 49 patients + 26 HC = 75 total enrolled for neuroimaging but exact analyzed n varies by contrast. Values assigned to n_analyzed in contrast entries are estimates based on reported group sizes.

No MNI coordinates are provided in Table 4 (or anywhere else for FC results). Clusters are identified only by brain region names from the AAL atlas. No coordinate triplets are available for any FC result.

Table 4 reports 'Clusters' as integer indices (1, 2, 3, etc.) per comparison and 'Brain regions' listing multiple regions per cluster. It is ambiguous whether each cluster index corresponds to one spatially contiguous cluster or multiple regions within a cluster. Regions within each cluster number have been concatenated in brain_region_exact.

The paper does not explicitly report within-group changes in FMA from baseline to 2-week follow-up as numeric values. Patients were classified into MCID/N-MCID based on these changes, but mean/median change scores per group are not provided in a table.

The note in Table 3: 'Negative t-test values reflect significantly more DC in identified regions of interest for the MCID group.' Thus negative t values = MCID > N-MCID; positive t values = N-MCID > MCID for DC comparisons.
This study does not include a sham acupuncture control arm. All patients and healthy controls received real acupuncture at GB 34. There is no placebo or sham intervention.
Supplementary Table S1 is referenced for additional demographic/clinical information but was not provided with this PDF.
